title: Ada and the Inheritance
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Voss is exhumed for a heritage ceremony and found empty, true-crime podcaster Jude Blackwood is summoned by Ada Voss, the founder's last living descendant, whose family trust — and her life — hinge on proving what happened to the body. As Jude digs into a 70-year-old disappearance, he discovers the case file has been quietly edited over decades by someone still alive and still protecting the secret. The killer, now elderly and embedded in the town's institutions, begins eliminating everyone who touched the original investigation. In the end Jude traps the killer with a staged exhumation of a second grave, and Ada must choose between exposing the truth that destroys her inheritance or burying it to save the man she has come to love.
about_author: G. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering cold cases in New England before turning to fiction. They live in a converted gristmill with two indifferent cats and an unhealthy interest in cemetery records.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Jude Blackwood, mid-recording on his podcast about unsolved cases, watches as the coffin of founder Edmund Voss is opened for a centennial ceremony and found empty. The crowd's shock turns to suspicion when Jude is recognized from his podcast. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: professional excitement curdling into dread as he realizes this case will consume him.

chapters.title: The Last Voss
chapters.summary: Ada Voss visits Jude's studio, revealing that the family trust requires proof of Edmund's death; without a body, she loses everything. She offers him full access to the Voss archives. Jude notices she flinches at one name in the family ledger: Harlan Pike, the town's current patriarch. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: wary attraction shadowed by the sense that Ada knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Seventy Years of Silence
chapters.summary: In the archive basement, Jude reconstructs the original 1954 investigation: Edmund vanished the night of the founding gala, and the case was closed within a week as 'voluntary departure.' The lead detective's notes end abruptly mid-sentence. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt, undercut by the uncanny neatness of the file — too tidy, as if curated.

chapters.title: What the Ground Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude interviews the groundskeeper who dug the grave decades ago; the old man recalls the coffin being 'lighter than it should be' even then. That night someone ransacks the archive, taking only the 1954 coroner's report. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: first real fear — the past isn't sleeping, it's being guarded.

chapters.title: Harlan Pike's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Ada takes Jude to meet Harlan Pike, ninety-one, charming and terrifying, who warns them off with a smile: 'Some inheritances are burdens, Miss Voss.' Jude finds a photo of young Harlan at the 1954 gala beside the missing detective. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the corrupting weight of old power made flesh.

chapters.title: A Voice on Tape
chapters.summary: Jude releases a cautious episode and receives an anonymous call: a woman claiming her father was the coroner's assistant and left a sealed letter before his death. She agrees to meet but never arrives. POV: alternating Jude and Ada. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into guilt — speaking into a microphone has consequences.

chapters.title: The Edited File
chapters.summary: Comparing a 1970s microfilm copy against the modern file, Jude proves the case record was altered at least three times, each edit erasing evidence pointing toward the quarry outside town. Only someone with institutional access could have done it. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the killer didn't evade the system; the killer runs it.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Divers search the flooded quarry and find a 1950s pocket watch engraved E.V., plus human remains too degraded to identify quickly. The town erupts; Harlan calls an emergency council meeting. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: vindication tangled with terror as she becomes the public face of a scandal.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: At the emergency meeting, Jude watches the town's elders close ranks, rewriting history in real time. He recognizes the pattern from his research: the same families, the same reflexes, seventy years apart. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: disillusionment — the mystery isn't one murder, it's a machine that manufactures silence.

chapters.title: The Coroner's Letter
chapters.summary: The anonymous caller's father's letter surfaces, mailed before her disappearance: it names a second person present at the quarry in 1954, initials H.P., and mentions 'the girl.' Jude realizes there may have been a witness no one ever counted. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: grief and urgency — the letter cost a life.

chapters.title: What Ada Knew
chapters.summary: Confronted, Ada admits her grandmother left diaries suggesting Edmund planned to expose the town's founding fraud — land deeds built on stolen territory — and that Harlan's father helped silence him. She withheld this to protect the trust. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: shame and rupture; love against duty fractures between them.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Following the diaries, Jude locates an unmarked plot behind the old chapel holding the remains of the 1954 lead detective — murdered, not retired. The killer has been tidying graves for seventy years. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into resolve; the pattern finally has edges.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Someone runs Jude's car off the road; he survives with a concussion and a partial plate number traced to a vehicle owned by the Voss Trust — meaning someone inside Ada's circle, or Ada herself, is compromised. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: paranoia; every ally becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Trustee
chapters.summary: Jude investigates the trust's longtime trustee, Margaret Ellery, who has managed Voss affairs since 1962 and signed off on every file access. Her alibi for the caller's disappearance is airtight — because she wrote it. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the quiet satisfaction of cornering a careful mind.

chapters.title: Confession at the Mill
chapters.summary: Margaret, confronted privately, reveals she is the coroner assistant's daughter — the anonymous caller's aunt — and has spent fifty years inside the machine trying to undo it, editing files to leave breadcrumbs rather than erase them. POV: Margaret via recorded conversation. Emotional beat: tragic complicity; the corrupted system corrupted its own saboteur.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Gala Photograph
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing Margaret's breadcrumbs, Jude identifies 'the girl': a housemaid, sixteen in 1954, who saw the killing and was shipped away under a new name. Records show she died last year — but not before donating papers to a historical society under an alias. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: mourning a stranger who held the whole truth.

chapters.title: The Witness Papers
chapters.summary: In the historical society's vault, they find the maid's sworn account naming both Harlan's father and young Harlan himself as present at the quarry. But the pages are copies — the originals were requested 'for authentication' three weeks ago. By whom? POV: Jude. Emotional beat: racing dread; the killer is ahead again.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Study
chapters.summary: They trace the request to Harlan's estate and find his study burned the night before, Harlan hospitalized for smoke inhalation — or staged. At his bedside, Harlan whispers that he didn't kill anyone, but he knows who did, and 'she'll finish the ledger.' POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the ground shifts; the monster may be a dying man's shield.

chapters.title: The Ledger-Keeper
chapters.summary: Jude deduces the true killer: Margaret's own brother, the town archivist, who has spent his career curating the Voss legend and has begun destroying anyone who disturbs it — including his sister. He lures Ada to the chapel crypt with a forged note in Jude's name. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: terror and betrayal converging in the dark beneath the church.

chapters.title: Crypt
chapters.summary: Climax: In the crypt, the archivist forces Ada to help him seal the witness papers inside Edmund's empty coffin forever — completing the erasure. Jude arrives with police and Margaret, who talks her brother down by confessing their father's role aloud. The archivist breaks, and Ada chooses to hand over the papers, forfeiting the trust. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — Ada chooses truth over inheritance.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Edmund Voss's recovered remains are laid to rest; the town confronts its founding fraud in an unflinching final episode of Jude's podcast. Harlan dies peacefully, leaving his estate to fund the historical society's honest archives. Margaret retires, unrepentant and relieved. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure; some justice costs everything it touches.

chapters.title: Ada and the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Ada, stripped of the trust but free, opens a small museum of the town's real history. She and Jude, having chosen each other over the cases that consumed them, record one last episode together — then turn the microphones off. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: quiet hope; the truest inheritance is the story told honestly.
